newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German state says building costs too high.
newsitem.headline: East German state says building costs too high.

text.p: A German state finance minister involved in one of the country's most ambitious rebuilding projects said on Friday that construction was being hampered by prohibitively high costs.

Speaking at a construction industry conference in the eastern city of Leipzig, Georg Milbradt, finance minister for the state of Saxony, said new building and financing methods were required to make construction affordable.
"Construction is simply too expensive...It cannot go on like this," said Milbradt, who has a role in funding the billion-mark redevelopment of the former Communist-controlled eastern state of Saxony.
He said Germany lay far behind the United States and Japan in the degree of automisation involved in the construction process, while too little risk was being taken on the financing of projects.
East German firms were moreover still unable to afford minimum wages across the industry set out by new laws, he added.

Milbradt's comments follow the decision of the Transrapid high-speed rail consortium last month to part company with German building firms originally due to build the infrastructure and open the project out to open tender in a bid to save building costs.
Milbradt said new financing schemes involving private funding were required but said the state should not withdraw from its obligation to invest in large projects.
"The state must fulfil its role as an investor and as an institution that shapes the future," he said.
The rebuilding of eastern Germany that followed German unification in 1990 has been financed to a large degree by financial transfers from the west of the country to the east.

Even with such redevelopment, Germany's construction industry is still locked in recession. The Association of the German Construction Industry said earlier it expected building investment this year to fall 2.2 percent in real terms.
